title: Rental Agreements
text:
A rental agreement is a legal contract between a landlord and a tenant. It sets out the rent, the length of the lease and the rights of both parties. Before signing, tenants should read every clause carefully, because a verbal promise is often hard to enforce in court.

The contract may also include a termination clause, which explains how either side can end the agreement early. Many agreements require a notice period of one or two months. If one party breaks the terms, the other may seek compensation through the courts.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, why should tenants read every clause carefully?
options: Because verbal promises are often hard to enforce in court
Because the rent is always negotiable
Because the landlord must sign it in front of a notary
Because the lease can never be shorter than a year

questions.text: According to paragraph two, what does a termination clause explain?
options: How either side can end the agreement early
How many tenants can live in the flat

questions.text: What can be inferred about a tenant who relies only on a verbal promise?
options: They are automatically protected by the law
They may have little legal protection if the promise is broken
They must pay a higher rent

questions.text: Why does the author mention a notice period?
options: To show that agreements are always short
To suggest that ending a contract usually requires advance warning
To prove that landlords never end contracts
To explain how to calculate the rent

vocabulary.definition: to make sure that a rule or law is obeyed
a single part of a legal document that deals with one specific point
a person who pays rent to live in or use a property
money paid to someone to make up for loss or harm

paragraph_translations: Umowa najmu to wiążący prawnie kontrakt między wynajmującym a najemcą. Określa czynsz, długość najmu oraz prawa obu stron. Przed podpisaniem najemcy powinni dokładnie przeczytać każdą klauzulę, ponieważ ustną obietnicę często trudno wyegzekwować w sądzie.

Umowa może także zawierać klauzulę rozwiązania, która wyjaśnia, jak każda ze stron może zakończyć umowę przed czasem. Wiele umów wymaga okresu wypowiedzenia wynoszącego jeden lub dwa miesiące. Jeśli jedna ze stron złamie warunki, druga może dochodzić odszkodowania przed sądem.
